Immune-mediated deforming arthropathy affecting joints and periarticular connective tissues.
Congenital cranial nerve synkinesis causing eyelid ptosis during jaw opening.
Mesenchymal kidney tumor occupying and replacing renal parenchyma.
Open spinal neural tube defect involving spinal neural structures and failure of vertebral arch closure; renal injury is not universal.
Inherited carnosinase deficiency; seizures, intellectual disability and developmental regression are annotated in 80-99%. Carnosinuria does not establish renal damage.
Disease of skeletal muscle fibers causing impaired muscle function and weakness.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal damage frequency in this specific late-infantile form is insufficiently established.
BACH2-related immunodeficiency and autoimmunity. Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis and infection-related bronchiectasis are separately diagnosed associated diseases.
PAX9-related absence of permanent teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital retinal dysfunction causing stationary night blindness and reduced visual acuity; nervous-system ancestry does not establish extraocular disease.
Vaginal epithelial tumor affects a reproductive organ outside the axes; intestinal differentiation does not indicate gastrointestinal origin.
Female reproductive system malignancy; reproductive organs have no axis, and spread to other organs is not universal across this umbrella.
Severe neurodevelopmental impairment, characteristic skeletal abnormalities and congenital heart disease define the syndrome; renal malformations occur in roughly 30-50%.
Central movement disorder with generalized and orofacial dyskinesia; feeding problems and hypotonia do not establish separate gut or muscle damage.
Absent thumbs/radii 3/3; renal agenesis and esophageal atresia/TEF each 2/3. Hydrocephalus 2/3 and other CNS abnormalities omitted by the four-axis cap.
BH4 synthesis disorder causing central neurotransmitter deficiency, typically dystonia or encephalopathy; neurologic dysfunction defines symptomatic disease.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting limbs, epiphyses and femoral necks. Broad or short nails are morphological findings without demonstrated functional damage.
Umbrella disorder of the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes; neither cutaneous disease nor infection applies across most subtypes.
Glycosylation disorder defined by skeletal dysplasia and psychomotor delay; hepatomegaly 4/4 with raised ALT 3/4. Thrombocytopenia 3/4 omitted by cap; renal disease 1/4.
Malabsorption 80-99%; skeletal abnormalities 30-79%. Cataract and vocal-cord paresis 30-79% omitted by cap; hepatomegaly and hair changes lack demonstrated dysfunction.
Bone fragility, osteoporosis and fractures; syringomyelia and intraventricular hemorrhage each reported in 1/2 patients support CNS involvement, with limited sample size.
Acquired skeletal myopathy with myosin loss, severe weakness and muscle atrophy; sensory and cognitive functions are spared.
